summary: The root بَسَسَ (bassa) primarily means to crumble or break something into small pieces, like dry bread or flour. It also refers to driving away or scattering things, such as camels.

headwords.def: بَسٌّ بس signifies The act of breaking: or breaking in pieces: syn. حَطْمٌ. (TA.) [And The act of mixing: see بَسِيسَةٌ. This, or the former, is probably the primary signification.] [And hence, app.,] بَسَّهُ, aor. بَسُسَ, inf. n.

بَسِيسَةٌ بسيسه بسيسة Wheat, &c., broken, or crumbled, or bruised: (Msb:) or سَوِيق [or meal of parched barley or wheat ], and flour, &c., mixed with clarified butter, or with olive-oil: (M:) or what is stirred about with olive-oil, or with clarified butter, and not wetted [with water ]: (Lh, M:) or سويق, or flour, or ground أَقِط, stirred about, or moistened, with clarified butter, or with oliveoil; (S, K;) after which it is eaten, without being cooked: (S:) or سويق, and flour, moistened with…

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
